A billboard for Apple featuring a young child holding an iPhone has drawn criticism in Italy, prompting the country's child rights watchdog to refer the ad to three regulatory bodies. Here's what happened.

Apple's "Relax, it's iPhone" ad campaign has drawn criticism in Italy

Italy's Autorità Garante per l'Infanzia e l'Adolescenza (AGIA) has expressed concern over an Apple billboard in Milan showing a young child holding an iPhone, accompanied by the tagline "Tutto ok, è iPhone."

The ad is part of Apple's long-running "Relax, it's iPhone" campaign, which typically showcases the iPhone surviving environments where it could potentially be damaged.

The latest billboards in the series have shown the iPhone being used in heavy rain, knocked off a table by a cat, and carried in a dog's mouth.

One of the new billboards features a young child holding an iPhone — seemingly making the point that parents need not worry even if their child drops the device. But AGIA has labelled it as normalising the "electronic babysitter," sparking controversy.

AGIA said in a press release that the matter was brought to its attention by a citizen in Milan, who said the image was "disturbing" because it "brings together two worlds that should remain separate."

AGIA said it has referred the case to Italy's communications regulator AGCOM, the Italian competition authority AGCM, and the country's advertising self-regulatory body IAP, "for appropriate examination and any potential action."

Apple has not publicly responded to the matter at this time.
